_comment: The block decoder's bounds checks, removed one at a time. tests/test_compress.cpp hands the decoder streams built by hand to overrun each one -- a length past the declared size, a token claiming more literals than the input holds, an offset before the start, a stream cut off inside a sequence -- and requires not just a corruption status but the one that check produces, since a check that is gone can leave a later check to refuse the stream after the out-of-bounds read has already happened. The encoder is covered by the round trips. Not here: the in-loop room check in read_extra, which only stops a run of 255s early; with it gone the post-check refuses the same streams with a different message, so a mutant is equivalent for the decoder's answer and the check is defence in depth. The wide copies: a match copied eight bytes at a time from less than eight behind repeats bytes it has not written yet, and the round trips see it; literals copied wide with no room past them in the output overwrite the string's terminator, which the test built for it reads. The two room checks left -- a wide copy reading past the end of the input, and a match spilling past the end of the output -- change no byte of the result when removed, so they survive a plain build and are caught by a build with AMBAR_SANITIZE=address, which is what the (sanitizer) in their names means; see mutations/README.md.
